# WaveStar NMPC source reference convergence diagnostic

The `source_*.npz` files preserve 4,501 samples of independent 225 s
MATLAB R2025b WaveStar NMPC runs from [Python-repository CI run
39883276159](https://github.com/cmudrc/wec-sim-python/actions/runs/39883276159)
and its [repeat run
39886232300](https://github.com/cmudrc/wec-sim-python/actions/runs/39886232300).
They are **diagnostics, not accepted physical parity references**. Each run's
three source artifacts contain the original body/PTO CSV files and controller MAT
files. `convergence.json` and `convergence_rerun.json` record the full
source-to-source comparisons in the two runs.

The workflow pins WEC-Sim `0753b2e47f2457c078751dcfe5d251d1767b80ab`,
Applications `d53d4d4c9eda2581f04204f5d394a6ef84bb099e`, and the exact
`wavestar.h5` in
[`../wavestar_nmpc_split_step_225s`](../wavestar_nmpc_split_step_225s/README.md)
(SHA-256 `b2541ff01c319987d9157d1be9fbc9ec39a7660d0572d8e316c428b8aa3359d1`).
The 500 wave components match that pinned fixture exactly. All runs use the
`ode4` source plant, the same 50 ms controller and output interval, and plant
steps of 1, 0.5, or 0.25 ms. Only disposable Applications input files were
configured for the runs; no changes were pushed to either MATLAB repository.
The NPZ arrays are float64 copies of exported source time, pitch, pitch
speed, PTO stroke and speed, axial force, requested torque, and components.

| Comparison | Max pitch gap | Max request gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Older pinned 1 ms vs fresh 1 ms | 0.010596 rad | 0.792728 N m |
| Fresh 1 ms vs 0.5 ms | 0.009193 rad | 0.573686 N m |
| Fresh 0.5 ms vs 0.25 ms | 0.004763 rad | 0.450018 N m |
| First vs repeated 0.25 ms | 0.012014 rad | 0.732573 N m |

The original pointwise limits are 0.0005 rad pitch and 0.1 N m request.
The older and fresh 1 ms source pitches agree to `2.29e-15` rad through
15.2 s, then separate after NMPC activation. The first 15.2 s pitch gaps
between the fresh 1/0.5 and 0.5/0.25 ms runs are `2.6722e-5` and
`1.3348e-5` rad; smaller plant steps have not delivered an acceptable full
closed-loop target. Independent physical Python, run at the matching plant
step with only the exact HDF5 and generated sea phases driving feedback,
differs from the 0.5/0.25 ms source traces by up to 0.006714/0.009435 rad
pitch. The 0.25 ms pitch-peak aggregate gap is 0.7149%, over its 0.5% limit.
These first matched-step Python checks ran locally on macOS ARM64 with NumPy
2.5.4 and SciPy 1.18.1. In the repeat Linux run, the two 1 ms and two 0.5 ms
source exports reproduced exactly at their respective steps. The 0.25 ms
source exports agree within `1.10e-15` rad pitch through 15.2 s, but differ
by up to `0.012014` rad pitch and `0.732573` N m request over 225 s despite
the same HDF5 hash, sea components, source revisions, and step settings.
The repeated 0.25 ms source is `source_0p25ms_repeat.npz`; its matching Linux
Python pitch gap is `0.011711` rad and the pitch-peak aggregate gap is
`0.7851%`. Both exceed the original limits. The earlier pinned 1 ms trace
also differs from both standalone 1 ms runs, although those standalone runs
match each other numerically. This record does not isolate which runner or
source setup detail caused the difference.

A [single-thread repeat](https://github.com/cmudrc/wec-sim-python/actions/runs/39891127477)
held [MATLAB's computational thread limit](https://www.mathworks.com/help/matlab/ref/maxnumcompthreads.html)
at one in two fresh 0.25 ms runs. Both used R2025b Update 7, the exact HDF5,
the same sea components, and identical source revisions. The Intel Xeon
Platinum 8573C run reproduced `source_0p25ms_repeat.npz` exactly; the AMD EPYC
9V45 run reproduced `source_0p25ms.npz` exactly. Their pitch and request gaps
remain `0.012014` rad and `0.732573` N m. The matched independent Python
pitch gaps are `0.011711` and `0.006740` rad respectively, both beyond the
pointwise limit. [`single_thread_repeat.json`](single_thread_repeat.json)
records the numerical comparison, MATLAB versions and thread counts, and
runner CPU details. This associates the two source trajectories with the
tested CPU models despite one MATLAB computational thread; it does not
identify the exact CPU-dependent operation.

The two single-thread controller logs also permit a 0–40 s frozen-input
probe. [`single_thread_controller_probe.json`](single_thread_controller_probe.json)
was generated by
[`wavestar_nmpc_controller_source_probe.py`](../../../../tools/wavestar_nmpc_controller_source_probe.py),
feeding each source's logged observer states and AR forecast to an independent
Python QP. Its maximum Python-versus-corresponding-source request gaps are
`0.000136` and `0.000085` N m. The two source requests themselves separate by
`0.196588` N m within 40 s, and the two Python replays reproduce that
separation to within `8.84e-8` N m at its 39.55 s maximum. This rules out a
large Python QP replay mismatch in this early window; it does not identify
which upstream floating-point operation first perturbs the closed loop. The
logged AR forecasts already differ by up to `17.77` N m at 10.4 s, during the
resistive startup interval when the forecast does not drive the command.

A [compatible-BLAS repeat](https://github.com/cmudrc/wec-sim-python/actions/runs/39894739858)
then used [MathWorks' MATLAB override](https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/2066506-how-do-i-make-matlab-use-the-mkl_cbwr-environment-variable-as-the-cnr-branch)
and [Intel's common code branch](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/onemkl/developer-reference-c/2026-0/getting-started-with-conditional-numerical.html).
Both source jobs reported R2025b Update 7, one computational thread, and
oneMKL 2024.1's `CNR branch compatible` in `version -blas`. Both happened to
run on AMD EPYC 7763. Their full 225 s exported pitch, speed, stroke, force,
and request traces match numerically exactly; the compact
[`source_0p25ms_compatible_amd7763.npz`](source_0p25ms_compatible_amd7763.npz)
and [`compatible_repeat_summary.json`](compatible_repeat_summary.json)
preserve that result and its audit. This is a same-CPU repeat, so it does not
show that compatible BLAS removes the Intel/AMD source difference. The
[`compatible_controller_probe.json`](compatible_controller_probe.json) also
finds identical logged observer states, AR forecasts, and source requests
through 40 s; Python's frozen-input QP request stays within `0.000012` N m
of each source. The
independent physical Python run at the same 0.25 ms plant step misses every
pointwise limit: its maximum pitch gap is `0.017938` rad versus `0.0005`
rad, and its requested-torque gap is `0.937424` N m versus `0.1` N m. The
pitch-peak aggregate gap is `0.6762%` versus `0.5%`. This source can be used
to diagnose the Python discrepancy on that CPU, but it is not an accepted
portable physical parity baseline.

The Python repository's
[`wavestar-nmpc-reference-convergence.yml`](../../../../.github/workflows/wavestar-nmpc-reference-convergence.yml)
regenerates the MATLAB exports, audits autonomous physical Python, and
compares the source traces. A source target that passes across supported CPU
classes, a step-convergence argument, and a passing independent physical
pointwise gate are still required before issue #623 can close.
